evidence.quote: Like the other aerodynamic force, drag, the lift is directly proportional to the area of the object.
Doubling the area doubles the lift.

concepts.name: Lift is directly proportional to area

evidence.quote: the logical choice is the wing planform area.
The planform area is the area of the wing as viewed from above the wing, looking along the “lift” direction.

concepts.name: Wing planform area as reference area

evidence.quote: designers try to increase the wing area.
This is done by sliding the flaps backwards along metal tracks and shifting the slats forward to increase the wing area.

concepts.name: Flaps and slats increase wing area for takeoff and landing

objectives: Explain that lift is directly proportional to object area
Identify wing planform area as the reference area for lift
Describe how flaps and slats increase wing area during takeoff and landing
analysis.unsupportedReason: The source covers how lift varies with wing area, planform reference area, and flap and slat deployment, but it does not teach the full lift equation relating lift to coefficient, density, and velocity.
